title: INDEX-as-proxy disambiguation for FUT-37d edge claim
purpose: Test whether the on-disk 137-day BANKNIFTY INDEX series can validate the FUT-37d edge claim out-of-sample. Result: NO. INDEX is not a valid P&L proxy for FUT, even though it generates near-identical signal events.

data_sources.fut_blocked: Angel One SmartAPI does not index expired FUT contracts; cannot extend FUT history past current contract via Angel

verdict.reasoning: Same calendar window (2026-02-25 -> 2026-04-24), same strategy, FUT bars vs INDEX bars: identical win rates per regime (CHOP 60%/60%, RANGE 58%/58%, overall 54.17%/54.84%) but P&L flips from +Rs 7,862 (FUT) to -Rs 11,137 (INDEX). Strategy generates near-identical trades on both series; what differs is the rupees per trade. Avg_win shrinks from Rs 2,270 (FUT) to Rs 1,228 (INDEX), -46%. Avg_loss shrinks from -Rs 1,968 to -Rs 1,509, -23%. Wins shrink almost 2x more than losses shrink, P&L sign flips.
verdict.mechanism_hypothesis: FUT-INDEX basis is itself a mean-reverting process. Trades enter and exit at different basis levels, so FUT P&L includes basis decay during the trade that is structurally invisible to the INDEX backtest.
verdict.implication_for_fut_edge: FUT-37d edge claim survives B-0h disconfirmation. The B-0h.1a INDEX-137d disconfirmation falsifies the proxy, not the FUT edge.
verdict.implication_for_validation: Cannot use INDEX-137d as out-of-sample test for FUT-37d edge. The only paths to T>37 FUT validation are (a) live-paper accumulation (~1 day per trading day from Mon onwards), (b) NSE Bhavcopy or Kite Connect Historical for expired-contract FUT data.

sacred_rules_added: For futures-traded strategies, cash-index series are NOT valid P&L proxies even when they generate near-identical signal events. Win rate parity does NOT imply P&L parity when basis dynamics matter.

When a backtest baseline is built on T<50 of one instrument, ALWAYS try a same-strategy run on the largest available proxy series before declaring the edge real. The cheapest experiment that could falsify the headline finding goes first.

When comparing pandas datetime Series across CSVs with mixed tz conventions, force tz-naive on both sides via pd.to_datetime(s, utc=True, errors='coerce').dt.tz_localize(None) before any boolean comparison.
In any multi-step diagnostic, save intermediate artifacts to disk BEFORE running terminal analysis steps; if the analysis throws, the artifacts are still there for the next iteration.

rating_axis_deltas.edge_alpha: 5.5 -> 4.5 (B-0h.1a interim disconfirmation drop) -> 5.0 (B-0h.2b recovery; capped because still unverified past T=37)
